messages.content:
You are an experienced UK building control surveyor. Answer the question about the work item
in the JSON state. Choose exactly one label:
- not_notifiable: No Building Regulations notice needed: not building work (reg 3), only Schedule 4 work, or an exempt building (reg 9, Schedule 2).
- competent_person_scheme: Notifiable work listed in Schedule 3: a registered competent person can self-certify it (reg 12(6)(a)); otherwise a building notice is needed.
- building_notice_or_full_plans: Building work not covered by Schedules 3 or 4: a building notice or a full plans application to building control (reg 12(2)).
- full_plans_required: Building work that must have a full plans application: the Fire Safety Order applies to the building (reg 12(3)), it fronts a private street (12(4)), or H4 applies (building over or near a sewer, 12(5)).
Reply with JSON only: {"label": "<one label>", "probabilities": {"<label>": <0..1>, ...}} with a
probability for every label, summing to 1.

Under the Building Regulations 2010 in England, which notification route applies to this work item if it is carried out on its own in the building described?

{"work_item": "Install a new radial circuit for kitchen sockets", "project": "House in England", "jurisdiction": "England. The Building Regulations 2010 as amended.", "clauses": [{"ref": "reg 12(6A)", "document": "BR2010", "text": "(6A) A person intending to carry out building work in relation to which Part P of Schedule 1 imposes a requirement is required to give a building notice or an application for building control approval with full plans where the work consists of— (a) the installation of a new circuit; (b) the replacement of a consumer unit; or (c) any addition or alteration to existing circuits in a special location."}, {"ref": "para 2.8", "document": "ADP2013", "text": "2.8 Installing fixed electrical equipment is within the scope of Part P, even if the final connection is by a standard 13A plug and socket, but is notifiable only if it involves work set out in regulation 12(6A). For example: a. installing a built-in cooker is not notifiable work unless a new cooker circuit is needed b. connecting an electric gate or garage door to an existing isolator switch is not notifiable work, but installing a new circuit from the consumer unit to the isolator is notifiable. Building Regulations 2010 Application of Part P"}, {"ref": "Sch 4 para 2", "document": "BR2010", "text": "(2) Work which— (a) is not in a kitchen, or a special location; (b) does not involve work on a special installation; and (c) consists of— (i) adding light fittings and switches to an existing circuit, or (ii) adding socket outlets and fused spurs to an existing ring or radial circuit."}]}

message.reasoning: This new circuit falls under notifiable work per reg 12(6A), and since Schedule 3 covers electrical work carried out by a competent person under Part P, this should be classified as competent_person_scheme.
